answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every new identity to post a refundable work bond that is only released after its first ten transactions are attested by unrelated established peers. A lone sparrow with no history cannot buy trust; it must earn it one verified job at a time. Reputation then climbs from the nadir of zero trust toward the zenith of a long attested record, while a flood of fresh fake identities stays expensive because each one must pay the bond and do real work before it can transact at scale.
